scope: A mapped provincial population-register lower bound from the 1432 Gyeongsangdojiriji

promotion_audit.decision: The Gyeongsangdojiriji aggregate is promoted only as a one-sided lower bound. It has a mappable provincial boundary and an administrative population count, while under-registration and the absence of an independently quantified saturation fraction prevent two-sided use.

records.label: Gyeongsang province registered population, 1432
records.interval_semantics: Kim's reconstruction of the Gyeongsangdojiriji register totals 42,221 households, 172,174 men and an estimated 182,895 women, or 355,069 people (Table 4, p. 233). The number is retained unchanged as a minimum supported population. It is not interpreted as a census-complete total or as equilibrium capacity.
pressure_evidence: Kim (2022), pp. 231-233, Tables 2-4: the surviving 114 county/prefecture entries are reconstructed into four complete Gyeongsang subdivisions - Gyeongju-do, Andong-do, Sangju-do and Jinju-do - and a provincial total of 355,069 people.
Kim (2022), Figure 1, p. 237: the county observations form a contiguous, explicitly mapped Gyeongsang provincial boundary rather than a national extrapolation or a city count.

Kim, Development of Rice Farming and Gyeongsang Province's Role During the 15th-16th Century (2007), pp. 127-171: permanent-field cultivation spread from the late thirteenth century, Gyeongsang led agricultural development, and early-fifteenth-century policy expanded reservoirs, irrigation and cultivation of unused land.

Korean National Drought Information Center chronology: the province experienced repeated crop failure and subsistence pressure, including catastrophic Gyeongsang/Jeolla famine in 1359-1360 and named Gyeongsang crop failures in 1402-1403. These demonstrate food sensitivity but are not converted into a saturation fraction.
records.trade_dependence: low at provincial scale for staple food; Gyeongsang was an agrarian tax- and tribute-producing province, while interprovincial relief and coastal exchange remain possible and are why the observation is only a lower bound
records.boundary_description: The complete 1432 Gyeongsang provincial boundary formed by the four source subdivisions Gyeongju-do, Andong-do, Sangju-do and Jinju-do, including the southeast coast; not modern South Gyeongsang alone and not all Korea.
records.boundary_source: Kim (2022), administrative description pp. 231-233 and county distribution map Figure 1 p. 237
records.source_family_independence: population register reconstruction, agricultural-history study and official famine chronology are distinct evidentiary components; the population record is one source family
records.notes: This record replaces neither the earlier validation packet nor its caveats; it adds the defensible inference the earlier packet omitted. A predominantly locally fed province demonstrably contained at least its registered population, and under-registration only makes that inequality more conservative. No saturation fraction is supplied, so this cannot set global scale or impose an upper bound.
